content.user_title: Write Formal Chinese With Precise Meaning
content.value_statement: Informal Chinese can weaken clarity and alter evidence boundaries. This skill rewrites it as professional Chinese while preserving facts, structure, terminology, and conclusions.
actual_capabilities: Rewrites informal Chinese as formal, direct, professional prose.
Preserves facts, numbers, dates, units, conclusions, and evidence boundaries.
Keeps code, SQL, configuration, logs, commands, and quotations unchanged.
Standardizes terminology, status labels, and references across a document.
Clarifies unknown causes, unverified relationships, and unsupported conclusions without increasing certainty.
Maintains headings, tables, analysis frameworks, and page structure.
limitations: It does not verify factual accuracy or validate cited evidence.
It asks for clarification when ambiguity could change the intended meaning.
It does not translate between Chinese and other languages.
It cannot invent missing data, measurements, causes, or conclusions.

use_cases.title: Polish Project Updates
use_cases.description: Convert informal progress notes into clear status updates while preserving confirmed results and unresolved issues.

use_cases.title: Prepare Technical Reports
use_cases.description: Standardize terminology, evidence levels, tables, and process descriptions in technical Chinese documents.

use_cases.title: Refine Client Deliverables
use_cases.description: Turn draft Chinese content into concise, professional text suitable for external delivery.

prompt_templates.title: Rewrite a Short Note
prompt_templates.prompt: Rewrite the following text as formal Chinese. Preserve every fact, number, and conclusion. Return only the final text: [paste text]
prompt_templates.scenario: Beginner request for a short message or note

prompt_templates.title: Polish a Project Report
prompt_templates.prompt: Polish this project report in formal Chinese. Keep the headings, lists, tables, dates, metrics, and status labels unchanged in meaning: [paste report]
prompt_templates.scenario: Structured document with several content types

prompt_templates.title: Standardize Terminology
prompt_templates.prompt: Rewrite this document in formal Chinese and use these approved terms consistently: [term list]. Preserve code, commands, quotations, and field names exactly: [paste document]

prompt_templates.title: Preserve Evidence Boundaries
prompt_templates.prompt: Produce a formal Chinese version of this analysis. Separate confirmed facts, unknown causes, unverified relationships, and unsupported conclusions. Do not increase certainty or add evidence: [paste analysis]
prompt_templates.scenario: Advanced analysis with sensitive evidence levels

best_practices: Provide the complete source text and its intended audience.
List approved project terms and status labels before requesting a rewrite.
Mark uncertain claims and evidence levels explicitly in the source.
anti_patterns: Do not request invented facts, causes, metrics, or conclusions.
Do not omit context when a phrase has several possible meanings.
Do not use the skill to verify evidence or factual accuracy.

faq.question: What content can this skill rewrite?
faq.answer: It rewrites reports, status updates, analyses, tables, and other Chinese business or technical documents.

faq.question: Does it change the original meaning?
faq.answer: No. It preserves facts, structure, data, conclusions, and evidence levels while improving expression.

faq.question: How does it handle ambiguous text?
faq.answer: It requests clarification when ambiguity could affect meaning. It does not convert uncertain language into confirmed claims.

faq.question: Will it modify code or commands?
faq.answer: No. It keeps code, SQL, configuration, logs, commands, and original quotations unchanged.

faq.question: Can it follow project terminology?
faq.answer: Yes. User-approved terms and existing project terms take priority over general terminology.

faq.question: Does it check whether claims are true?
faq.answer: No. It improves language but does not verify facts, sources, calculations, or evidence.
